title: The secret life of a dental nurse
html:
In the latest episode of Aura Infection Control’s podcast series with Dentistry, a panel of professionals reveals what life in the dental nurse role is really like.

The conversation begins with stories submitted by dental nurses, from sedated patients and escaped spiders to flooded practices and awkward conversations.

The panel shares its reactions, along with a few embarrassing moments of its own.

One panellist recalls a heavily pregnant receptionist misunderstanding a patient who asked for her number. Another remembers her unborn baby kicking a patient in the head during treatment.

However, the episode is about much more than mishaps. The discussion moves on to the moments that make dental nursing rewarding, including qualifying, supporting nervous patients and helping trainee nurses develop their careers.

‘It’s really special when you have a really nervous patient or you’ve witnessed their journey from being extremely nervous to coming out of their shell,’ says Harriet Gill, dental nurse and TikTok influencer.

The panel also reflects on the challenges dental nurses face. These range from learning unfamiliar instruments and procedures to coping with inspections, a lack of career support and the disruption caused by the COVID-19 pandemic.

More than ‘sucking up the water’

A key theme throughout the episode is how little those outside dentistry may understand about the role.

Dental nurses support clinicians, care for patients, manage decontamination and help to keep the day running. Despite this, their work can sometimes be reduced to one visible task.

‘You’d get comments like: “Oh, so you’re the one who sucks the water out of my mouth.” I do a lot more than that,’ says Chontelle Roberts, sales and service consultant at Aura Infection Control.

The panel also discusses the importance of finding the right practice and having a supportive team.

‘When you find the right place for you, you’ll just feel settled and you’ll want to progress there and enjoy going to work,’ says Harriet.

Topics explored include:

  • Dental nurses’ funniest and most embarrassing moments
  • The best and most difficult parts of the role
  • Supporting nervous patients
  • Career development and opportunities
  • Common misconceptions about dental nursing
  • Inspections, career support and the impact of COVID-19
  • Finding the right practice and a supportive team
  • The responsibilities behind the dental nursing role.
